question: What rules and numbers do the throwable, explosive, mine, launcher and supply gadget graphs hold?

sourceFacts.method: Compiled expression graphs were listed with expression-graphs/exgraph.py (format from L4016, names from L4017 and L4019) and read section by section by a delegated reader; each constant cited here was then checked at its raw offset in the resource file. Full reading: expression-graphs/findings/gadgets-explosives-supply.md.

control.description: Every cited constant is a raw-offset check against the resource body. Function meanings marked inferred in the findings file are not relied on for the checked values.

points: Claymore (`SimEx_ClaymoreFrag`): damage = BaseDamage x pellets x sprint modifier x range term x (0.67 if the target's armour is above 0), rounded to steps of 5. Pellets come from PelletCount, a stance factor and distance, with constants 2.3 and 25, clamped to PelletLimit. A -3 offset enters the range term. The tunable values themselves are not in the graph.
Supply crate (`SimEx_SupplyCrate_Granite`): tick period 5 s (floor 0.01); each tick applies a per-weapon-class ammunition affector with parameter 4.95; the target must have health above 0.

Flashbang, Stun Drill and Stun Drill trigger flash share one rule: effect class from view angle (in front, sides, behind) and close or far range, six duration tunables, plus 0.2 s, through `Affector_Flashbang`.
Concussion grenade: three rings (close, mid, max radius tunables), each with its own duration tunable and its own entry of `Affector_ConcussionGrenade`.
PTKM1R: only vehicles faster than `VehicleMovingThreshold` and between MinimumRange and MaximumRange trigger it; scan period 0.1 s; an owner-state branch uses a 180 half-angle and 1.5 x MaximumRange.
Incendiary, thermobaric, proximity grenade and others are described in the findings file; those rows are a delegated reading and are not individually raw-checked.

inference: The Claymore constants 2.3 and 25 read as a spread angle and a density divisor; that interpretation is inferred from the arithmetic.
The Claymore range term passes through a function whose two end values are both 1.0, so range may be neutral in this build; unresolved.
Affector parameters are probably durations in seconds (4.95 s against a 5 s tick fits).
unresolved: Tunable values (ranges, radii, base damage) are named in the graphs but stored elsewhere.
Javelin lock-on rule: listing not readable.
The reader omits a call's jump target when it is not the next instruction, so some if/else shapes were read by pattern.
Which upgrade the PTKM1R owner-state branch tests.
siteImpact: None. No Analyzer data, simulation or UI change.

leads.title: Explosive and supply gadget graphs read: Claymore damage is a pellet-density formula with a 0.67 armour factor quantised to steps of 5, the supply crate ticks every 5 s with 4.95 s effects, flash effects add 0.2 s to a direction-and-range duration, and the PTKM1R scans every 0.1 s
leads.summary: About 35 gadget simulation graphs were read. Claymore damage is computed from pellet count, distance and stance, multiplied by 0.67 when the target has armour and rounded to steps of 5. The supply crate ticks every 5 s and applies ammunition effects with parameter 4.95. Flashbang and Stun Drill pick one of six durations by front/side/behind and close/far and add 0.2 s. The PTKM1R scans every 0.1 s for moving vehicles inside a range band. 14 raw-offset checks matched.
leads.reopenWhen: A gadget row is needed for a claim, or the tunable values are joined to these rules.
leads.statusNote: Explosive and supply gadget graphs read; headline constants raw-checked.
